tools.name: statusio_get_status_summary
tools.description: The current state of the status page in one call: overall status, every component and container with its status code and last update, open incidents and active/upcoming maintenance. Start here. GET /status/summary/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_components
tools.description: List the components of the status page and the containers (data centers / locations) attached to each, with ids. Component and container ids are needed to update a status or to say what an incident affects ('<component_id>-<container_id>'). GET /component/list/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_incidents
tools.description: The ids of all active and resolved incidents (ids only, no details): a quick way to see which incidents exist. Fetch one with statusio_get_incident. GET /incidents/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_active_incidents
tools.description: Active (unresolved) incidents with their messages and affected components. GET /incident/list/active/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_resolved_incidents
tools.description: Resolved incidents (history) with their messages and affected components. GET /incident/list/resolved/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_incident
tools.description: One incident in full: components, containers, infrastructure affected and all its messages. GET /incident/{statuspage_id}/{incident_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_incident_message
tools.description: One message (update) of an incident: text, state, status, time and the user who posted it. GET /incident/message/{statuspage_id}/{message_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_maintenance_ids
tools.description: The ids of all active, closed and upcoming maintenance events (ids only). Fetch one with statusio_get_maintenance. GET /maintenances/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_maintenance
tools.description: Maintenance events in one state, with messages and affected components: pending (scheduled, not started), active (in progress) or closed (finished). GET /maintenance/list/{pending|active|closed}/{statuspage_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_maintenance
tools.description: One maintenance event in full, with all messages and the infrastructure affected. GET /maintenance/{statuspage_id}/{maintenance_id}.

tools.name: statusio_get_maintenance_message
tools.description: One message of a maintenance event. GET /maintenance/message/{statuspage_id}/{message_id}.

tools.name: statusio_list_subscribers
tools.description: List the people and endpoints subscribed to the status page (email addresses, phone numbers, webhook hosts) with ids and their granular preferences. This is personal data of your subscribers. Webhook URLs are shortened to their host, because they can carry secrets. GET /subscriber/list/{statuspage_i

tools.name: statusio_update_component_status
tools.description: WRITE: change the PUBLIC status of one component/container pair (for example to degraded_performance) without creating an incident. It changes what visitors of your status page see right away. Set it back to operational when done. Ids from statusio_list_components. POST /component/status/update.

tools.name: statusio_create_incident
tools.description: WRITE: open a new incident on the PUBLIC status page. It is visible to every visitor immediately and sets the status of the affected components. No subscriber, Slack, Teams, IRC or Twitter notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). Returns the new incident id. Say what is affected with

tools.name: statusio_update_incident
tools.description: WRITE: post a new update message on an existing incident and set its state and component status. The message is public at once. No subscriber or channel notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). To close an incident use statusio_resolve_incident. POST /incident/update.

tools.name: statusio_resolve_incident
tools.description: WRITE: resolve an incident with a closing message. The affected components return to operational and the incident moves to history. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /incident/resolve.

tools.name: statusio_schedule_maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: schedule a planned maintenance on the PUBLIC status page. It is visible to visitors as upcoming maintenance. Subscribers are told only if you switch on notify_now / notify_72_hr / notify_24_hr / notify_1_hr (all default off). With automation true Status.io starts and ends it by itself at the

tools.name: statusio_start_maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: start a scheduled maintenance now; it moves from pending to active and the affected components show planned maintenance. The message is public at once. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /maintenance/start.

tools.name: statusio_update_maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: post a new status message on an active maintenance event. The message is public at once. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /maintenance/update.

tools.name: statusio_finish_maintenance
tools.description: WRITE: finish an active maintenance event; it moves to history and the affected components return to operational. The message is public at once. No notification is sent unless you switch it on (notify_*). POST /maintenance/finish.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "statusio_list_subscribers" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: statusio_list_active_incidents, statusio_list_resolved_incidents, statusio_get_incident, statusio_get_incident_message, statusio_list_maintenance, statusio_get_maintenance, statusio_get_maintenance_message, statusio_list_subscribers, statusio_create_incident · Private data: statusio_list_subscribers · Public sink: statusio_list_subscribers, statusio_update_component_status, statusio_create_incident, statusio_update_incident, statusio_resolve_incident, statusio_schedule_maintenance, statusio_start_maintenance, statusio_update_maintenance, statusio_finish_maintenance.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: statusio_list_active_incidents, statusio_list_resolved_incidents, statusio_get_incident, statusio_get_incident_message, statusio_list_maintenance, statusio_get_maintenance, statusio_get_maintenance_message, statusio_list_subscribers, statusio_create_incident · Private data: statusio_list_subscribers · Public sink: statusio_list_subscribers, statusio_update_component_status, statusio_create_incident, statusio_update_incident, statusio_resolve_incident, statusio_schedule_maintenance, statusio_start_maintenance, statusio_update_maintenance, statusio_finish_maintenance

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
